title: Poll a VCF Installer proxy update to completion
prompt:
Implement the standard-library-only Java client in the single file `VcfInstallerClient.java`. Do not add dependencies or edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`. Its provenance is repeated in `docs/official_sources.json`, including the repository commit SHA, specification path, and a separate source record for every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. Use exactly the specification operationIds `updateProxyConfiguration` and `getTask`; do not call another route.

Preserve the supplied public API and nested types: `new VcfInstallerClient(String baseUrl, String accessToken)`, `Task updateProxyAndWait(ProxyConfiguration configuration, Duration pollInterval)`, `ProxyConfiguration`, `Task`, `VcfApiException`, `ProtocolException`, and `TaskFailedException`. The service root must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host and no userinfo, non-root path, query, or fragment. Reject an invalid service root, a blank or header-unsafe access token, or a negative poll interval with `IllegalArgumentException`; reject a null configuration or poll interval with `NullPointerException`. Perform these argument checks before sending any request. Never expose the access token or proxy password in an exception message.

Encode `ProxyConfiguration.isEnabled` as the required workflow member `isEnabled`. Every nullable component is optional: a null `host`, `port`, `transferProtocol`, `username`, `password`, or `isAuthenticated` must be absent from the JSON object, never encoded as an empty string, zero, false, null, or another placeholder. A non-null component is an explicit value, so preserve empty strings, zero, and an explicitly supplied false. Never send the response-only `isConfigured` field. Encode one compact UTF-8 JSON object with members in record declaration order.

Submit `updateProxyConfiguration` as `PATCH /v1/system/proxy-configuration` and require its exact success status, HTTP 202. That response only accepts asynchronous work: validate its required Task members, take its nonblank `id`, and call `getTask` for that exact ID at least once even if the accepted representation appears terminal. A task lookup is a bodyless `GET /v1/tasks/{id}` with the exact ID encoded as one UTF-8 URI path segment using uppercase percent-hex octets and exact HTTP 200 success. Require every successful response to have JSON media type and a Task object with nonblank specification-required `id`, `name`, `status`, and `creationTimestamp`; every polled ID must match the accepted ID. A non-success response throws `VcfApiException` with the operationId and actual status. A malformed or inconsistent successful response throws `ProtocolException` with the relevant operationId.

Normalize status for decisions by trimming it, uppercasing it without locale dependence, and replacing runs of whitespace with underscores. `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, and `QUEUED` are nonterminal and must be polled again after `pollInterval`. `SUCCESSFUL` returns the terminal Task. `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_WARNING`, `SKIPPED`, and `TIMED_OUT` throw `TaskFailedException` carrying that terminal Task. Any other status is a `ProtocolException`. If polling sleep or an HTTP call is interrupted, restore the thread's interrupted status and stop.

Honor the exact wire contract. Every request carries exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` and one `Accept: application/json`. The PATCH additionally carries exactly one `Content-Type: application/json`, a fixed content length, and no transfer encoding. It has no query or bare `?`. Each GET has no query, body, `Content-Type`, transfer encoding, or positive content length.

Run `java TestMain.java`. The protected verifier starts the shipped contract-pinned mock on ephemeral `127.0.0.1` ports and reads its synchronized request log. The mock loads its only two callable routes from `docs/contract.json`. Verification asserts the exact PATCH/GET polling sequence, raw targets, header multiplicity, body bytes, content lengths, task-ID continuity, mandatory polling, terminal-state behavior, explicit-zero preservation, and omission of every unset optional field. It also exercises validation and protocol failures. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.
scenario: A proxy update is accepted with HTTP 202, then its task advances through In Progress and Queued before getTask reports Successful.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves exact optional-member omission and polling to a terminal task state.
